summary: Adversarial audit of the wave A simulation against the brief (REGLES_DU_JEU sections 2-7) and the contract readings, with 28 new tests in Tests/EditMode/Core/AuditTests.cs. Cross-rate tests run at 7 rates (30, 48, 60, 90, 120, 144, 240 Hz, all multiples of 6 so 1/6 s switch times stay on ticks). A property fuzz runs 6 seeded 40 s rounds of 4 deterministic roaming players with real turn rates, rings, lassos, wall runs, cuts, chases and eliminations. After every tick it checks the 10.1 invariants plus deeper ones: Pos inside Cell, R12 closed form, dead players clean, event times inside their tick and in order, sorted cells. At the end of each round it checks the counters against the events (Captures, CutsMade, Kills, PocketsMade), Exit/Return alternation, the R19 ranks rebuilt from FinalCells and EliminatedAt, the R1 rim band, and StateHash determinism on a twin run. Five real defects were found and fixed, each with the minimal change and every section 5 signature kept. FIX 1, Trail/Trail.cs (SelfCrossings) and Trail/LoopErase.cs, which is A4's open issue. Geo.ProperIntersect rejects a segment START inside the 1e-12 band of the old line but not a segment END (ta = 1 + 1e-16), so a self crossing that landed in the band at a tick end was lost by both ticks. The effects were no lasso and no LassoCrossNoCharge, and LoopErase kept the loop, so an uncharged return captured a self loop (against R8). Math/Geo.cs is outside A6's edit scope, so the new internal Trail.ProperCrossing wraps Geo.ProperIntersect with A4's symmetric end band, and SelfCrossings and LoopErase use it. Proven by R16_CrossingLandingInTheRoundingBandAtATickEndIsCountedExactlyOnce plus A4's 4 previously red S5/S6 tests, and by R16_NearMissAndSuperposedUTurnDoNotCountThenARealCrossingDoes, R17_ReturnCapturesPocketAndOrdinaryCaptureAsOneExactSetUnion and R13_CatchRightAfterALassoFollowsTheUnchangedArcLength. FIX 2, Sim/EventResolver.cs (BeginTick on the last tick). A cell edge reached exactly at t = RoundDuration can round to U = uEnd + 1e-15. On other ticks that entry shows up at U = 0 of the next tick, but on the last tick the return of the final instant was simply lost. Visit entries up to uEnd + 1e-9 are now kept and clamped to uEnd. Proven by R19_ReturnAndImpactBothExactlyAtRoundDurationTheReturnWinsAndCounts (no Return at all at 30 Hz before). FIX 3, Sim/EventResolver.cs (AddSparkCatch on the last tick). The eps shift pushed an impact with t_c in (RoundDuration - eps, RoundDuration] past the end, where no later tick fires it, so a caught player was ranked alive on its cells (against R13 and R19, and brief 6.4: resolve the events of that instant first). Such a catch now fires at uEnd, in the TimeUp group, and a return of that instant still wins. Proven by R19_SparkImpactExactlyAtRoundDurationEliminatesBeforeTheRanking. FIX 4, Sim/EventResolver.cs (AddPickup). n(u) was tested exactly, so two heads entering the ring at the same analytic instant from different directions (parameters 1e-16 apart) gave it to whichever rounded first, against brief 6.4 and Tuning.EventEpsilonSeconds ('closer than this are simultaneous'). A player now counts as in contact from in - eps/dt to out - eps/dt, while candidate times stay the true bounds. Proven by R15_RingEnteredAtTheSameInstantFromPerpendicularDirectionsIsContested. FIX 5, Sim/EventResolver.cs (StepReturns, CaughtBeforeReturn). The catch candidate already sits at t_c + eps, yet grouping by eps put a return made up to 2 eps after t_c in the same group, and step a saved the player. This violates R13 (t_r >= t_c + eps means eliminated), and only when both fell in one tick, so the outcome depended on the tick rate. A return whose own u is strictly after its own catch candidate in the group is now dropped; exact ties stay saved. Proven by R13_ReturnBetweenOneAndTwoEpsAfterTheImpactIsEliminatedAtEveryRate (saved at 30 Hz before). In a scratch copy with the 5 fixes reverted, 12 tests are red: A4's 4 S5/S6 tests and 8 audit tests. With the fixes, every test is green except A5's in-progress bot test (see open_issues). Everything else attacked held: exit and return inside one tick (a one-cell gap closing 32 cells); races decided across tick boundaries (catch root 0.5 eps before a tick boundary loses to a return on it, 3 eps before beats it); spark spawned and catching in one tick; R13b and R14 at all 7 rates; exposure-induced cut with s_cut = L - HeadGrace at all rates; held trailing head caught at the full SparkSpeed; wall slide while trailing (C3 at sim level, rim band neutral); last-cell loss while trailing with a pending spark; simultaneous eliminations of different causes sharing a rank; equal-s attacker tie; an attacker cutting from its own color; pocket cells contested by a simultaneous return; mutual stealing by two simultaneous returners (both TerritoryStolen, both return later on their current color); GR-Edge at the Simulation level; lattice corner ties; diagonal-edge flicker (harmless for the rules, see contract_issues). Full dotnet suite at the end: 267 / 268.

api_additions: No public member added. Internal only: Trail.ProperCrossing(Vec2d a0, Vec2d a1, Vec2d b0, Vec2d b1, out double ta, out double tb) = Geo.ProperIntersect plus the symmetric rounding band at the moving segment's end (shared by Trail.SelfCrossings and LoopErase.Erase). Private in EventResolver: LastTickSlack (1e-9 tick-u), ClampEntries, CaughtBeforeReturn.
contract_issues: 5.1 Geo.ProperIntersect (A4's finding, confirmed): the 1e-12 band is one-sided, applied to a0 but not a1, so a crossing that lands in the band at a tick end is counted by neither tick. Fixed on the Trail side (Trail.ProperCrossing). The 5.1 text should add: 'a1 within the same 1e-12 |b1 - b0| band of the line counts as reaching it at a1 (ta = 1, tb = projection of a1)'.

5.1 half-open rule versus brief 5.2 ('une tangence ... ne suffit pas'): 'a crossing exactly at the moving segment's end counts' also counts a pure touch. A charged head that lands exactly on an old segment at a tick end and then runs along it (or turns back) never reaches the other side, yet it spends the charge and gets a pocket. Probe at 30, 60 and 144 Hz: LassoPocket at t = 1/3 for a head going South onto the old segment y = H and then East along it. An old vertex touched by a V tip counts the same way (tb = 0 rule). This is measure zero with a finite turn rate and only reachable with lattice-aligned scripted paths (TurnRateDeg 0). Not changed: it is A1/A3 semantics fixed by 5.1. Suggested rule, if the user wants the brief strictly: decide a crossing on departure, i.e. count it when the head leaves the line to the side opposite to its arrival side (the arrival side is the last trail point off that line), in SelfCrossings and LoopErase together.

Section 6 grouping versus R13 (A4 had noted it): grouping by eps lets a return between t_c + eps and t_c + 2 eps share the catch's group, where step a saves it, but only when both fall in one tick, so the outcome depends on the tick rate. Fixed in EventResolver (CaughtBeforeReturn). Contract text for step a: 'a return whose own u is strictly after its own SparkCatch candidate in the group is dropped (step b eliminates)'.

Section 6 last tick: 'otherwise there is no candidate this tick (the max() makes it fire at the start of a later tick)' has no later tick at the end of the round, so impacts with t_c in (RoundDuration - eps, RoundDuration] were dropped and the victim was ranked alive. Likewise, a visit entry at uEnd + 1e-15 (an edge reached exactly at RoundDuration, rounded) dropped the final return. Both are fixed by a 1e-9 tick-u slack clamped to uEnd on the last tick. Contract text should say so, in line with R19 and brief 6.4.

Section 6 pickup: n(u) is defined exactly, but Tuning says events closer than EventEpsilonSeconds are simultaneous and brief 6.4 contests simultaneous touches. Fixed with an eps tolerance on the contact bounds (candidate times unchanged). Contract text should match.

R4 hold versus brief 2.3 ('le maintient contre le bord'): Arena.Step returns p0 when the step would leave the inset within 10 degrees of the normal, so a held head stops up to one full step short of the inset line (0.2 u at 30 Hz, 0.1 u at 60 Hz, 0.042 u at 144 Hz). Its stop position, its trail and captures next to the wall therefore depend on the tick rate (the runtime uses 60 Hz, so this is minor). Suggest stepping to the inset line and then holding. World/Arena.cs is A1's, not changed.

Captures counts empty returns (section 6 step a: 'Captures++' per returner): a home player gliding along its own 45 degree staircase edge produced 67 Exit / Return pairs in 2 s, every one capturing 0 cells (R7_GlidingAlongAnOwnDiagonalEdgeFlickersHarmlessly). That inflates PlayerState.Captures, hence the HumanOutcome stats line and the section 9 bot targets ('averages >= 5 captures'). Each flicker is also a full Exit + Return event pair, so the Runtime would play pearl detach / merge visuals and sounds at about 30 Hz (B2, B5), and each return is one CaptureSolver call. The rules themselves hold: the flicker trail never leaves HeadGrace, so it is never exposed and nothing is captured. Decision for the contract owner: count Captures only for returns with Cells.Length > 0 and let views ignore empty sub-cell returns, or switch to an 8-adjacency rim (A2's suggestion).
open_issues: Full dotnet suite at the end: 267 / 268. The red test is A5's Bots_UnchargedBotNeverCrossesItsOwnTrail(6UL) ('the excursion that ended at t=26.85 captured nothing'). A5 was editing BotTests.cs and BotController.cs while A6 ran (06:04-06:05). The same failure, at the same instant, appears in a scratch copy with all 5 A6 fixes reverted, so it is unrelated to them; it may be the empty diagonal-edge flicker returns described in contract_issues.

Unity EditMode was not run by A6 (not required by the task). AuditTests.cs is a new file, so Unity generates its .meta on the next run. NUnit features used: Test, Assert.That with Is.EqualTo/Within, Is.InRange, Is.GreaterThan, Is.LessThan, Is.GreaterThanOrEqualTo, Is.LessThanOrEqualTo, Assert.AreEqual, IsTrue, IsFalse, TestContext.WriteLine (confirmed in Unity's NUnit 3.5 by A3). Also used: System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch (logging only, no timing assertion) and SortedSet. Under UNITY_5_3_OR_NEWER the fuzz runs 2 seeds instead of 6. In dotnet Debug the audit class takes about 8 s (fuzz about 5 s).

Geo.ProperIntersect itself still has the one-sided band (Math/Geo.cs is A1's and outside A6's edit scope). Trail.ProperCrossing compensates for SelfCrossings and LoopErase, but any future caller of Geo.ProperIntersect would still see the defect.

Flicker cost measured in R7_GlidingAlongAnOwnDiagonalEdgeFlickersHarmlessly: 0.239 ms per tick on average in dotnet Debug, for one gliding player on a 12720-cell territory (about 33 CaptureSolver calls per second). Four players gliding on large territories could take several ms per tick on Android. B6's probe should measure it.
The tangency-at-tick-end rule (contract_issues 2) is left as specified by 5.1, pending a user decision.

Decide the tangency-at-tick-end rule (brief 5.2), whether Captures counts empty returns and how views treat sub-cell flicker exits, and the R4 hold stop position.
